shortDescription: Dispensers keep a bucket instead of throwing it out when there is nothing to pick up or place
oneLiner: A dispenser that can't use its bucket — empty bucket with no fluid in front of it, or a water bucket aimed at a solid block — keeps the bucket instead of throwing it on the floor, so an automated water door survives a misfire.

configKeys.effect: Play vanilla's "dispenser failed" click when a bucket is held back instead of thrown; false keeps a repeatedly triggered dispenser completely silent.

events: net.neoforged.fml.event.lifecycle.FMLCommonSetupEvent — mod event bus, lambda listener added in DispenserBucketGuardModule.onInitialize (line 50); the actual registry write is deferred via event.enqueueWork(this::installGuards) because DispenserBlock.DISPENSER_REGISTRY is a plain non-concurrent map (a fastutil Object2ObjectOpenHashMap with defaultReturnValue(DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR), which the module's own comment calls a HashMap) that must not be written from the parallel mod-loading thread
notes:
PROVEN FROM SOURCE (re-verified independently, including against the decompiled vanilla 1.21.1 sources in build/neoForm/neoFormJoined1.21.1-20240808.144430/steps/patchUserDev/output.jar).

FILES (complete module, three classes): modules/dispenser_bucket_guard/DispenserBucketGuardModule.java, .../BucketDispenseGuard.java, .../config/DispenserBucketGuardConfig.java. Plus standalone/dispenser_bucket_guard/DispenserBucketGuardStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_dispenser_bucket_guard"), boots via StandaloneModuleBootstrap). Registered in the bundle at VanillaPlusAdditions.java:183 (import at :48); standalone entry at build.gradle:421 with no dataGlobs, no moduleDeps, no mixins and no clientMixins keys.

NO MIXIN, NO ACCESS TRANSFORMER, NO REGISTRY OBJECTS. vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json has no dispenser_bucket_guard entry, there is no mixin/dispenser_bucket_guard/ package, no DeferredRegister anywhere in the module, no compat/ directory, no JEI plugin, no ModList.isLoaded and no shouldInitialize override -> requiredMods and optionalMods are genuinely empty. No lang keys (grep for "dispenser" over en_us.json and over src/main/resources as a whole returns nothing; the only "bucket" hit is flying_fish_bucket, which belongs to another module). No TODO/FIXME, no dead code.

HOW IT WORKS. At FMLCommonSetupEvent (enqueued onto the main thread) installGuards() iterates a *copy* of DISPENSER_REGISTRY.entrySet() and replaces every entry whose item is a BucketItem or SolidBucketItem with a BucketDispenseGuard wrapping the previous behavior. Already-wrapped entries are skipped (`behavior instanceof BucketDispenseGuard`), so guards cannot stack. Wrapping instead of replacing preserves whatever another mod registered for the same item.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRAPPED IN VANILLA 1.21.1 (verified in DispenseItemBehavior.bootStrap): the empty BUCKET (its own behavior, pickup branch), WATER_BUCKET and LAVA_BUCKET, the six mob buckets COD/SALMON/PUFFERFISH/TROPICAL_FISH/AXOLOTL/TADPOLE (MobBucketItem extends BucketItem, all carry Fluids.WATER -> placement branch) and POWDER_SNOW_BUCKET (SolidBucketItem, which extends BlockItem and does NOT extend BucketItem, so the two instanceof branches in wouldSucceed are disjoint).

PREDICTION IS READ-ONLY. Vanilla's own checks mutate on success (pickupBlock drains the block, emptyContents places the fluid), so BucketDispenseGuard.wouldSucceed mirrors them without touching the world:
- BucketItem whose `content instanceof FlowingFluid` -> placement branch: `state.isAir() || state.canBeReplaced(content) || (state.getBlock() instanceof LiquidBlockContainer c && c.canPlaceLiquid(null, level, pos, state, content))`. That is verbatim the `flag1` computation at the top of BucketItem.emptyContents; the NeoForge vaporize branch and the ultra-warm branch below it only run *after* flag1 is true, so they cannot change the prediction.
- BucketItem whose content is NOT a FlowingFluid (Items.BUCKET carries Fluids.EMPTY) -> pickup branch: `state.getBlock() instanceof BucketPickup && (state.getBlock() instanceof PowderSnowBlock || state.getFluidState().isSource())`.
- SolidBucketItem -> `level.isInWorldBounds(front) && level.isEmptyBlock(front)`, which is exactly SolidBucketItem.emptyContents' own condition.
- anything else -> returns true (delegate untouched). The guard can therefore only ever PREVENT an ejection, never cause one.

THE PICKUP PREDICTION IS EXACT FOR EVERY VANILLA BucketPickup. The four implementations are LiquidBlock (yields iff LEVEL == 0, i.e. iff the fluid state is a source), SimpleWaterloggedBlock (yields iff WATERLOGGED, which is also exactly when getFluidState() is a water source), PowderSnowBlock (always yields - hence the explicit instanceof) and BubbleColumnBlock, which also always yields but whose getFluidState() returns Fluids.WATER.getSource(false), so `isSource()` covers it. No vanilla block is mis-predicted.

KNOWN LIMITS / GOTCHAS A DOC WRITER MUST KNOW
1. ASYMMETRIC RUNTIME TOGGLE. The enabled check sits per dispense (DispenserBucketGuardModule.isActive() inside dispense()), so turning the module OFF at runtime takes effect immediately. But if the module is disabled at STARTUP the wrapper is never installed at all, so turning it ON later needs a restart. docs/modules/dispenser_bucket_guard.md states this; the README paragraph does not.
2. LATE REGISTRATIONS ARE MISSED. Only entries present in DISPENSER_REGISTRY at FMLCommonSetupEvent are wrapped. A mod that registers a bucket dispense behavior after common setup is not guarded (no re-scan exists).
3. MODDED BucketPickup THAT YIELDS WITHOUT A FLUID SOURCE is mis-predicted as "nothing to pick up" -> the bucket is held back although vanilla would have picked something up. This is the one case where the module changes a *working* outcome. Workaround per the module doc: disable the module.
4. emptyContents failing AFTER its placement check (setBlock refused and the old state was not a source) is not predicted -> vanilla ejects as before.
5. MILK BUCKET is untouched twice over: Items.MILK_BUCKET is a MilkBucketItem extends Item (not a BucketItem at all) and it has no dispense behavior registered, so it is never in the registry and is thrown like any other item.
6. THE GUARD ROUTES BY ITEM TYPE, NOT BY THE REGISTERED BEHAVIOR. A modded BucketItem whose content is not a FlowingFluid takes the *pickup* branch even though it is a filled bucket (vanilla's emptyContents returns false for such buckets anyway, so vanilla would always eject). More generally, a mod that registers a non-fluid dispense behavior for a BucketItem/SolidBucketItem gets fluid semantics applied to its prediction.
7. FAIL-OPEN STATICS. `playFailSound()` returns true when `instance == null`; `isPlayFailSoundValue()` returns true when the ModConfigSpec value is null (config not yet loaded). `isActive()` returns false when instance is null, i.e. the guard delegates to vanilla.
8. SINGLE STATIC INSTANCE. `DispenserBucketGuardModule.instance` is assigned in the constructor, so the last-constructed instance wins. Harmless in the bundle (one registration) and in the standalone jar (one @Mod), but the guard's static lookups are not per-instance.
9. HARDCODED SOUND EVENT ID. `FAIL_SOUND_EVENT = 1001` is a literal int with a comment pointing at LevelEvent.SOUND_DISPENSER_FAIL; the vanilla constant is not referenced.
10. `canPlaceLiquid(null, ...)` passes a null Player deliberately - that mirrors the dispenser path, which also has no player and no BlockHitResult (hence no neighbour fallback).
11. VPA'S OWN flying_fish_bucket IS NOT COVERED. It is a MobBucketItem, but no VPA module calls DispenserBlock.registerBehavior (grep over src/main/java finds no registration outside this module), so it is not in the registry and a dispenser throws it exactly as before.

CONTRADICTS THE REPO AS IT STANDS
- README.md:118 and README.md:303 link to `docs/dispenser_bucket_guard.md`, which does NOT exist. The file lives at `docs/modules/dispenser_bucket_guard.md` (the docs/ reshuffle is staged in the working tree, the README links were not updated). Both links are currently broken.
- CHANGELOG.md:205 also still says "Doku: `docs/dispenser_bucket_guard.md`" (historical entry, arguably fine to leave).

VERIFICATION EVIDENCE IN THE REPO: CHANGELOG 1.0.0-beta.79 and docs/modules/dispenser_bucket_guard.md both describe an A/B test on a throwaway headless 1.21.1 server, six cases, same command script with and without the module: the three ejecting cases flip to "kept", the two working cases give a byte-identical dispenser inventory (water_bucket after pickup, bucket after placement), and a snowball still leaves the dispenser. That is a claim recorded in the repo, not something re-run here.

SIDE CAVEAT: "server" is the honest answer for behavior - all logic runs on a ServerLevel (BlockSource.level() is a ServerLevel), dispensers only fire server-side, and there is no rendering, no keybind and no Minecraft.getInstance() anywhere in the module. FMLCommonSetupEvent itself fires on both physical sides, so the wrapper is technically installed in a client's registry too; it is just never invoked there.
